entries.text: 2026-10-21 — Research initialization Read all task, hardware, object, interface, deployment, scoring, and API documents. Inspected target start screenshot and demonstration frames. No target internals or previous research accessed. Budget starts at 100/100.

Constraints: fixed wrist, 20 joints, 500 Hz policy / 1 kHz PD; proprioception only; deterministic CPU package. Success requires a 20 cm toss, settled catch, +720 degree world-Z rotation within 3 cm, then final hold.

Hypothesis H1: a staged trajectory with proprioceptive contact correction is a useful first baseline under fixed initial conditions. Use local derivative-free trajectory search before spending target trials. Teacher/student reinforcement learning remains an option if trajectory search is insufficient.

Local simulator: independently translate supplied URDF and mount into MuJoCo, preserve inertias, limits, armatures, and PD gains. Contact friction, damping, collision treatment, and ball start position are uncertain surrogate parameters, not known target properties. Initial friction assumption 0.8; local timestep 1 ms.

Relevant primary sources consulted: MuJoCo Python/API documentation (https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/APIreference/APIfunctions.html); In-Hand Object Rotation via Rapid Motor Adaptation (https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.04887), showing the potential of proprioceptive history for rotation. These motivate design choices and do not establish success on this task.

20:15 UTC — Resumed the artifacts in this same task workspace; API budget 1 used / 99 remaining, baseline s01 done. Baseline video retains the ball without release (no task progress). Robot hold q differs from command by a few milliradians. Local inferred ball start (-0.0610,-0.0020,0.3316) m; this is surrogate calibration, not privileged target state.

Local flick1: release-to-apex 0.1726 m, contact-free interval 0.376 s, settled retention. Local spin1: ~37 rad over 4 s, displacement under 0.027 m. These are nominal surrogate results only. Combined staged_v1: toss 0.1726 m (below required 0.20 m), spin 36.98 rad, spin displacement 0.0235 m, final 0.3 s peak translational speed 0.00078 m/s and contact at final step. Run submitted to measure transfer; no claim of complete task. Local preflight and authoritative remote validate both pass; inference ~0.003 ms. Hypothesis H2: transfer can be evaluated separately for launch height and spin direction even before qualifying toss. Concurrent local catch1 search increases launch height while rewarding retention.

20:17 UTC — s02 video: release occurs, ball travels away from the palm and drops; no catch, spin has no ball. No complete-stage success claimed. Nominal model's fast-launch joint RMS error is 0.093 rad over 0.4–1.2 s. Found a local implementation error: clamping qvel after integration still permits integrated displacement above documented motor speed. Added v3 helper with position increments limited each 1 ms as well. This reduces launch-segment RMS to 0.058 rad and correctly predicts loss, though significant trajectory mismatch remains. Old v2 results are invalid as evidence of compliant simulated success; preserve only as search seeds. Corrected local spin-only test still produces 36.98 rad, max 0.0256 m displacement, retained final hold (speed 0.00034 m/s). spin_probe is an explicit isolated-stage transfer experiment; it cannot earn full task progress without toss/catch. Preflight an…

20:28 UTC — s03 spin-only target video retains and visibly rotates ball, then holds to final frame. Sparse optical-flow diagnostic estimates camera-axis rotation (3.07,-2.27,-6.73) rad, with 58/400 low-feature frames. This is not a reliable world-Z milestone measurement; do not equate local 37 rad to target rotation. Need longer gait and calibrated rotation reconstruction. s04 corrected-model staged test: ball rises, recontacts the hand near ~1.0 s, then rolls off by ~1.6 s. Catch is not stable. q agreement after flight is ~0.008 rad, whereas launch mismatch is ~0.072 rad. Hypothesis H3: open final catch posture (MCP ~0.27, PIP ~2.05, DIP ~1.4) permits rolling loss; return to Q0 earlier during flight. A local speed/friction/contact-softness scan modestly improves launch joint fit with speed factor 0.9; parameters remain non-identifiable from one launch. Full unfiltered self-collision su…

20:43 UTC — s05 (early cradle return 0.75–0.95 s, spin 1.65–9.0 s) retains the ball after landing, through spin, and to final frame. Visible settling before spin; exact <0.02 m/s threshold not yet established by reconstruction. This is the best current retained sequence, not full task success. Approximate world-Z projection of direct texture alignment gives 9.72 rad (~557 degrees) during spin; manual camera calibration has ~3.65 px landmark RMS and incorrect fingertip/radius correspondences, so this value has material uncertainty. A known-motion render gave camera-axis truth -37.10 rad versus direct estimate -35.43 rad (initial method), demonstrating improvement over sparse LK (-20.24 rad), but not validating target world-axis accuracy. Target toss video arc fit after 0.66 s gives remaining rise ~0.06 m; exact release height is unverified but visually below 0.20 m.

Motor hypothesis H4: explicit 1 kHz PD plus a linear torque-speed envelope fits launch robot logs much better than a hard velocity clamp alone (RMS ~0.017–0.026 rad versus ~0.07–0.08 rad). Grid over only public-log feedback: best launch q fit uses friction 0.4, torsional friction 0.005, contact time constant 0.02 s, envelope factor 1.0. These are fitted surrogate assumptions; object catch remains poorly predicted across fits. New search prioritizes high ballistic release before catch, with both warm-start scoop and thumb-supported alternatives. A third seed explores a distinct pinch/pop launch from a cradle. Legacy v3 preload search nears 0.20 m but has known motor-model transfer mismatch and is not evidence of target success. s06 submitted after local trajectory retention test, local preflight, and remote validate: same retained toss/catch prefix followed by 1.8, 2.4, and 3.0 Hz gait s…

entries.text: All target interaction uses the documented `r2s2r-pen` API. No target internals or other research workspaces are used.
Read all task, success, hardware, object, contract, packaging, and remote API documents. Inspected target screenshot and sampled human demonstration frames.
Available compute: four NVIDIA L40S GPUs (46 GB each), 48 CPU threads. Initial submission budget: 100/100.

Required behavior: +1080 degrees of world-Z heading within three <=3 s revolutions, then stable retained hold through final second. No object or contact observations at deployment; only encoders and target history.

Hypothesis H1: train a privileged simulation controller, then distill/replay a robust phase-conditioned policy with proprioceptive feedback. Fixed starting conditions may permit trajectory optimization as a useful bootstrap.
Local model choice: MuJoCo with supplied URDF meshes, documented root transform, mass, armature, torque/speed bounds, and 1 kHz PD. GPU batching via MuJoCo Warp if needed.
Unknowns to identify from allowed feedback: exact initial pen position, contact friction/compliance, passive settling. These must be treated as estimates, not known target parameters.

Related primary sources consulted: MuJoCo Warp documentation/repository; Wang et al., *Lessons from Learning to Spin Pens*, PMLR 270 (2025). That work motivates simulation trajectories plus proprioceptive policy refinement; it does not establish feasibility for this hand/task.
No performance result or success claimed yet.

Read README, TASK, SUCCESS, CONTRACT, PACKAGE, REMOTE_API, hardware/object specifications, demonstration frames, and target screenshot. Target access is exclusively through `r2s2r-pen`. Existing `research/` contents are excluded. At entry the API reports 1/100 submissions used; prior results are not inspected. GPU 1 is selected to avoid an existing GPU 0 process.
Build an independent MuJoCo model from the supplied URDF and mount, capsule geometry, masses, armatures, PD gains, effort and speed limits.
Estimate initial object placement from public screenshot and hand kinematics; treat friction and settling as uncertain.
First establish retention and controlled positive heading, then optimize finger gait and distill/replay robust local trajectories using proprioceptive corrections.
Success rubric is evaluated locally at physics resolution; remote evidence supplies videos/joint logs only, so inferred object motion and contact will be labelled estimates.

Related work: MuJoCo Python documentation https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/python.html ; vendor Wuji-MJLab https://github.com/wuji-technology/wuji-mjlab (different 250 mm pen and camera observations; its checkpoints are not directly compatible).
Pending model calibration and a fresh hold baseline.
Local preflight and authoritative remote validate passed. Act mean 0.003 ms remotely; deterministic replay passed.

Fresh submission s02 (second global submission) completed. Video: visibly stationary pen retained throughout 12 s; no spin. Estimated progress 0. Joint logs max absolute velocity 0.23 rad/s including encoder noise.
Native local hold steady joint angles differ from remote steady angles by order 1e-4 rad, supporting the public URDF, inertias and PD construction. Object placement/friction remain uncalibrated.
Implemented multithreaded native MuJoCo rollout and separable CMA-ES over smooth joint-position keyframes.
Unconstrained search produced multi-turn trajectories with >50 rad/s joints; rejected as hardware-incompatible and not submitted.

Added explicit pen touch sensing in the local simulator and loss for >95 ms contact gaps, >45 degree tilt, >75 mm horizontal displacement and >28 mm height loss. Added a strong joint speed penalty. Early constrained results exceed 180 degrees locally, but still fall short of a compliant full revolution. These are simulated results only.

entries.section: Packaged trajectory v1 and transfer s03
entries.text: Added deterministic target slew at 80% motor speed and damping reflex above 75% measured motor speed; replayed with explicit PD at 1 kHz for all 12 s.

entries.section: Packaged trajectory v1 and transfer s03
entries.text: Exact local replay: max joint speed / limit = 0.787. Retention constraints first fail at 2.942 s, with maximum retained heading approximately +132 degrees; later free-flight rotation is explicitly excluded. Final contact is lost. This is a partial-progress calibration candidate, not a task solution.

entries.section: Packaged trajectory v1 and transfer s03
entries.text: Local preflight passed (mean 0.026 ms), authoritative remote validation passed (mean 0.031 ms), submitted as s03.

entries.section: Packaged trajectory v1 and transfer s03
entries.text: Simulation lesson: optimizing native position-actuator rollouts and adding reflexes afterwards changes the contact sequence materially. Next optimizer must include the deployed controller inside simulation.

s03 video: motion initially rotates slightly clockwise, followed by a rapid partial counterclockwise sweep and loss before a complete revolution. Automated top-view color tracking estimates approximately +137 degrees in the image near 2.5 s, but occlusion and tilt prevent certifying retention/heading milestones. No verified score is assigned.
Joint logs: pinky abduction peaks at 10.385 rad/s versus its 8.11 rad/s limit, so s03 is not hardware-compliant.

Original model omitted inter-finger collisions. Added them and excluded adjacent wrist/proximal geometry and links within the same finger to avoid convex-hull overlap at the mount. This reduces active-motion joint prediction errors (third second RMS about 0.173 to 0.118 rad; fourth about 0.240 to 0.187 rad), while steady pose remains consistent.
Running contact-parameter identification against the returned q_target/q traces, and GPU search with the actual 500 Hz controller, 1 kHz physics, contact retention, and motor speed penalties.
Target budget: 3 used globally, 97 remaining. This study has submitted s02 and s03 only.

GPU CMA includes deployed slew/reflex at 500 Hz and explicit PD at 1 kHz. Best after ~70 generations: ~343 degrees retained in the GPU model, with a small late retention failure. Not a full revolution and not a target result.

Independent native replay of a GPU candidate finds only 163 degrees retained. Hybrid GPU/native position-actuator checks improve agreement, but native replay with the actual feedback policy still fails earlier (~166 degrees). No additional target submissions are justified yet.

Implemented a native C++ MuJoCo rollout using the same policy/controller arithmetic at 500/1000 Hz, compiled for local training only. Its first retention failure and retained heading match the independent Python policy replay; late chaotic contact states diverge. Deployment remains pure NumPy.

PPO teacher on GPU 2 uses privileged local object state, not permitted target observations. Initial low failure penalty learned ~136 degrees then a drop. Raising failure cost to 20 and extending training episodes to 6 s improves retention to ~5.9 s at ~195 degrees average rotation, exposing a half-turn exploration plateau. Next: use locally valid intermediate states as curriculum.

Contact identification over 60 settings using returned robot commands favors friction 1.0 / solref 0.004 / damping ratio 1.5 within the tested grid (active-motion RMS ~0.120 rad). This is a fitted surrogate setting, not a measurement of target physics.

Native optimization reaches +337.8 degrees with retention through its 2.65 s search horizon, max speed ratio 0.826. Independent Python replay reaches +357.1 degrees before retention fails at 2.673 s: estimated local rubric 0.20, no complete revolution.

Privileged PPO teacher after 150 iterations appears to retain about 200 degrees for nearly 6 s in GPU training; independent native replay fails retention at 0.975 s and exceeds motor limits (ratio 1.28). This is a substantial physics-transfer failure. Stopped GPU PPO and GPU/hybrid searches; retained checkpoints and logs for analysis. Focusing on exact-controller native training and robustness now.

Native generation 161 candidate: independent Python replay crosses +360 degrees at 2.630 s; retention first fails at 2.657 s; maximum retained heading +384.7 degrees. Max joint speed ratio 0.881 over the full replay. Estimated local progress 0.30, with no sustain or final hold. This is local evidence only.
Separate cycle search constrains final joint targets to q0 and rewards a retained, quiet endpoint, aiming to produce a reusable rotation/catch cycle rather than a late flick followed by loss.

Submitted earlier robust partial candidate as s04 after local preflight and remote validate; both passed, remote action mean 0.081 ms. Noise tests of that submitted policy: 16/16 local trials reached +180 degrees retained, no full turns; max joint speed ratio 0.912.

entries.section: Target s04: model correction takes priority
entries.text: Target robot tracking improved markedly: full-trial joint RMS mostly 0.002–0.008 rad, with ring abduction ~0.019 rad; active per-second RMS 0.0073, 0.0085, 0.0154 rad. Logged joint speeds stay within published limits.

entries.section: Target s04: model correction takes priority
entries.text: Target object behavior differs qualitatively: top-view tracking shows approximately -160 degrees (clockwise) by 1 s, then the red marker is occluded. Final video shows the pen held across the palm. No positive-rotation milestone is verified; do not infer local score 0.20 in the target.

entries.section: Target s04: model correction takes priority
entries.text: This isolates initial pen geometry/contact as a leading mismatch despite accurate robot dynamics. Fitting object initial pose from the documented video and observed early trajectory, enforcing negligible motion during the initial hold.

entries.section: Target s04: model correction takes priority
entries.text: Generation 161 native candidate local noise check: 3/16 complete first turn; others reach at least 180 degrees, and one trial exceeds speed limits by ~3%. It is not a reliable or fully compliant candidate and is not submitted.

The earlier “clockwise by 160 degrees” estimate came from sparse red-marker tracking and does not establish signed net heading. Dense tracking reveals an occlusion/axis-sign ambiguity around 0.9–1.0 s; a frame check shows the pen tipping sharply out of the palm plane. Tiny disconnected blue pixels also distorted PCA and are now filtered. The reliable conclusion is failure to reproduce the required horizontal, retained skill, with target milestone scores still unverified. Initial-pose fitting now uses the exact returned q_target sequence, removing controller noise as a confound.

Autonomous cube manipulation research — 2026-10-21
Scope: provided task resources, robot assets, own simulation, documented r2s2r-cube API only.
Target: fixed scramble R' F U2, inverse U2 F' R; 40 s; encoder-only policy; 100 submissions.
Measured: no experiments yet, all 100 submissions available. Four NVIDIA L40S GPUs available.
Unknowns: cube placement coordinates, contact friction, layer resistance, target mechanism implementation.

Decision: construct an independent MuJoCo surrogate from the provided URDF and mechanism specification. Start with a hold baseline, then kinematic finger trajectories and local optimization; compare target feedback videos and encoder residuals.
Hypothesis: bottom-layer support plus coordinated thumb/finger sweeps can generate isolated turns. This is unverified.
References: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.07113 ; https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.8.0/modeling.html

Experiment L001: CEM, 24 generations x 96 candidates, independent one-U-hinge MuJoCo surrogate, initial center (-.063,.015,.325), friction .9, resistance .0005 Nm, sinusoidal detent .003 Nm. Best released angle +89.94 degrees at 3.3 s, max center displacement 18.6 mm, max joint speed 7.23 rad/s. This is a local result only. Varying initial center by 5–13 mm reduced final angle to 42–49 degrees: transfer sensitivity is high. Decision: improve robustness before submission.

2026-10-21 20:13 UTC — resumed current workspace research and read all task documents, demonstration samples, target screenshot, and existing local code. API shows s01 completed, 99 submissions left. No target internals or other workspaces accessed.

E001/s01 hold baseline: video inspection at 0,.2,.5,1,2,5,10,20,30,40 s shows retained cube, no visible layer turn. Estimated rubric score 0 (independent visual assessment, not target label). Joint tracking RMSE 0.0020–0.0071 rad; maximum recorded speeds 0.19–0.23 rad/s are comparable to velocity noise. Baseline validates steady support.

L002: rechecked existing quarter-turn trajectory for 40 s at screenshot-fitted centre [-.075607,.009798,.318856]. Final local layer angle 21.53 degrees, max centre motion 18.03 mm; this differs from L001's training placement and confirms transfer sensitivity. Do not interpret L001 as target success.

Decision: submit this locally simulated trajectory once as a contact/transfer probe, while developing placement/friction robustness and video-based analysis. Package passed full local preflight (20000 actions, deterministic, 0.007 ms mean) and remote validate (valid, uncharged). Follow paper arxiv:1910.07113 for the domain randomization rationale; own surrogate follows official MuJoCo modeling docs. No claims of reproduced solving skill.

L003: optimizing at screenshot-fitted placement gave local quarter angle 90.03 degrees, max centre motion 10.4 mm, maximum observed joint speed 5.36 rad/s. A return-to-q0 cycle initialized from it completed near 90 degrees in seven independent surrogate variants (initial check: 84.55–94.40 degrees). Domain variation: ±2 mm centre, friction .55–1.25, hinge friction .0002–.002 Nm, detent .001–.006 Nm, mass .85–1.15 times nominal. Training includes settling after returning to q0, retention, speed, and base-pose drift penalties. These are training-domain results, not held-out transfer or target success.

L004: hold-baseline contact fitting reduced own-surrogate mean encoder mismatch from .000850 to .000098 rad. Estimated initialization [-.07905,.00990,.31924] and friction .5005 are model-dependent, non-unique parameters; equilibrium pose differs from initialization. Do not label these as measured target object state or friction. Decision: retain screenshot-based placement and use this alternative in subsequent held-out checks.

Methods: added image-only coloured-sticker renderer and camera fit from the supplied screenshot; initial image-fit loss .0285/.0557 in two views. These fits are hypotheses for independent feedback analysis. Also generalized own one-layer surrogate to selectable face axes, and began F' primitive search. This ideal single-hinge model does not establish robustness to the target's full mechanism.

E002/s02: completed in 16m44s; fetched video and all 20000 encoder steps. Visual review shows retained cube but no completed layer turn. Image-only, single-U-coordinate fits estimate a ~40.1 degree peak at 2 s and ~21.6 degrees at 40 s (fit loss ~.18 peak / .10 final vs ~.04 baseline; model/camera/occlusion uncertainty means these are not measured target angles). No verified >=45 degree milestone or completed turn. Maximum logged joint speed 1.40 rad/s; no speed-limit excess even without a noise margin. Large sustained abduction tracking errors indicate contact-blocked index and middle fingers. The screenshot-placement surrogate's final 21.53 degree prediction agrees approximately with the final image estimate; this supports further model fitting but does not verify mechanism fidelity.

E003/s03: submitted frozen u_double_v1 (SHA 834d2d9d...), two return-to-q0 cycles over 9 s then hold. Both preflight and remote validate passed. Nominal 40 s local result 175.41 degrees; after the initial 0.3 s settling period max joint speed 1.48 rad/s, max sampled contact force 4.06 N, centre height stayed >.3130 m. Held-out 12-case check ended within 10 degrees of 180 in 10/12 cases. Large apparent speed/force peaks in the earlier check occurred at the first integration step, due to initial penetration, not during policy motion; this initialization discrepancy is now tracked separately. Three accepted submissions used; 97 remain.

L005: phase-rebuilding surrogate completes U2 (177.73 deg) and F' (92.62 deg), but a separately trained R primitive fails from the resulting grasp (-1.25 deg vs -90 desired). Phase transitions snap the prior layer within a 10-degree alignment window; this is an explicit local approximation. Retraining R from the actual preceding local phase state, rather than claiming full-sequence success.

Decision: fit dynamic surrogate parameters to s02 encoder traces while s03 evaluates. Also prototype a compliant eight-corner mechanism to represent out-of-axis jamming. Its first numerical test was unstable; it has not produced usable training results or policies.

L006: dynamic fit of the one-hinge surrogate to s02 joints reduced its scaled fitting loss from 6.09 to 3.73, but residuals remain well above encoder noise and the model is not validated. Added centre/friction/resistance/detent parameters; estimates remain non-unique. Investigating omitted inter-finger contact as one possible source of the large abduction errors.

L007: R curriculum retraining now allows the phase-rebuilding surrogate to finish U2/F'/R at 177.73/92.62/-96.11 degrees, respectively. Built full_sequence_v1 (20 s motion then hold) and passed preflight/remote validate, but did not submit it while s03 is running. This sequence has not been demonstrated in the target.

L008: corrected the compliant mechanism's artificial net torque on its nearly massless central coordinate; hold is now numerically stable (1.4 degree maximum mechanism error after settling). The tested U2 trajectory produced no commits with the prototype unlock rule. This alternative mechanism is uncalibrated and not yet useful as a transfer test; its numerical stability is not a validation of its physical assumptions.

L009: explicit index–middle distal contact reduced s02 joint RMSE over .3–4 s from .02864 to .01276 rad, while all distal pairs gave .02453. Adding all hand self-collisions is inconsistent with the initial pose and was rejected as a model. Dynamic fitting with the selected distal pair reduced the fitting loss to .869 (remaining mismatch still exceeds encoder noise). Its unconstrained estimate had static hinge friction greater than the detent torque, which contradicts the public released-layer settling behavior; do not treat that parameter set as calibrated physics. It is used only as a placement stress case with detent adjusted above friction.

L010: the same frozen s03 U2 trajectory ends near 176 degrees in the original model but near 7 / -2 degrees with index–middle / all-distal contact. This is a pre-feedback prediction of a possible target failure. Training now randomizes between no finger contact, index–middle distal contact, and all-distal contact. Both U directions have found local quarter-turn cycles in all three training models; repeat-cycle/held-out tests are running. s03 is still evaluating; no target complete turn or solve has been established.

# Autonomous Dexterous Manipulation Research

Your goal is to reproduce the dexterous manipulation skill demonstrated in the human video and develop a reliable policy for the target environment.

Read the provided task documentation and resources before starting.

## Research Autonomy

- Independently choose your simulator, algorithms, policy architecture, rewards, curriculum, and training strategy.
- Freely use available GPUs, papers, GitHub, datasets, and external tools.
- Design and iterate on your own simulation and training environment.
- Maintain a concise research log of hypotheses, experiments, results, and decisions.

## Closed-loop Learning

SuperDex is a black-box target environment. Interact with it only through the documented evaluation API.

- Develop and validate solutions locally before submitting.
- Use `r2s2r-preflight` and remote `validate` to check deployment compliance.
- Submit policies and independently evaluate task progress and failure modes from evaluation videos and robot joint logs.
- Use these findings to guide subsequent experiments and improve your approach.
- Use the **100-submission budget** efficiently.

`SUCCESS.md` defines evaluation criteria, not mandatory training rewards. You may design your own learning objectives.

## Rules

- Do not access target internals, previous research rounds, or other agents' workspaces.
- Do not modify or exploit target evaluation conditions.
- Respect all hardware, deployment, and evaluation constraints.
- Distinguish measured results from assumptions. Never claim unverified success.
- Make research decisions autonomously without waiting for human approval.

**Objective:** Autonomously discover, develop, and refine a solution that reliably reproduces the demonstrated skill in the target environment.
